gameStory.articleHeadline: Commanders snap Seattle's 12-game winning streak, beat the Seahawks 33-31
gameStory.articleDescription: — Two quarters after Washington linebacker Leo Chenal was carted off with a scary neck injury, backup Kain Medrano delivered the biggest play of the game.
gameStory.articleStory: LANDOVER, Md. -- — Two quarters after Washington linebacker Leo Chenal was carted off with a scary neck injury, backup Kain Medrano delivered the biggest play of the game. Medrano returned an interception 50 yards for a touchdown with 3:57 to play, and the Commanders held on for a 33-31 victory Sunday, handing the Seattle Seahawks their first loss since November. Marcus Mariota — another backup forced into duty — threw three touchdown passes for Washington, which forced three turnovers in its home opener. “One turns into two, two turns into three. Ball just falls that way,” Medrano said. “That momentum that we have, we're hunting the ball, and that's what we do as a defense.” Washington came into the game without linebacker Frankie Luvu, who was out with a groin injury. Chenal started, but then he went down late in the second quarter. It was a difficult moment — his teammates all came off the sideline to surround him as he was being tended to on the field. Coach Dan Quinn said after the game Chenal was at the hospital but had feeling in his extremities. “We're definitely thinking of him,” Quinn said. “He's a great teammate. We love him. Anytime a guy gets banged up like that, you're just thinking of him and pulling for him as much as you can." Without Chenal, Washington's linebackers were still a factor. whatToWatch.text: This defense is the story: 8.5 points allowed per game through two weeks, and they hit the road against a Washington team surrendering 30.5 a game. Something has to give — and Vegas thinks it's the Commanders, with Seattle laying 8.5.

A 40.5 over/under screams low-scoring slugfest, so every drive matters. Both teams are getting to the quarterback at the same clip (2.5 sacks per game), which means the unit that wins on third down probably wins the game.

Depth gets tested on both sidelines — five players out for Seattle, including Montorie Foster Jr., Jalen Milroe and Brandon Pili, and five out for Washington, with Frankie Luvu and Javontae Jean-Baptiste among them. Nobody's listed as questionable, so what you see is what you get: two shorthanded rosters, no excuses, 2-0 on the line.

recap.text: Seattle's winning streak died in Landover, and the killing blow came from a backup linebacker. Sam Darnold threw for four touchdowns — two to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, plus scores to Eric Saubert and Cooper Kupp — but his throw over the middle with under four minutes left landed in the hands of Kain Medrano, who took it 50 yards the other way to swing the game. The Seahawks coughed it up three times on the afternoon, and every giveaway fed a Washington defense that smelled blood. Darnold's late strike to Kupp pulled Seattle within two, but Marcus Mariota's three touchdown passes and Drew Stevens' foot had already built a cushion Washington never surrendered in the 33-31 loss.
